summary: Regression suite for the retrieval-live surfaces: the hook injection floor, the pointer page, find's Note: summaries, kb commit. Treat it as a CALIBRATION RECORD, not incidental coverage — several tests exist specifically to pin cases where ONE carrier must still inject (a code-shaped term like max_files, a converged term, a named path, the young-notebook exemption under 30 notes, a renamed anchor). Verified 2026-07-30: tightening the hook injection policy broke exactly those 7 and nothing else, which is how a too-blunt rule gets caught. A test here failing after a matcher change is evidence about the change, not noise. One caution observed: a positive assertion whose query carries a single prose word is implicitly testing the injection floor rather than its stated subject — the stemming test had that shape and now carries a second term from the note's own title so it still fails if stemming regresses.

summary: Live-corpus regression tests for retrieval: the hook injection floor (rarity gate, convergence override, path-name override), matcher repairs (stemming, HOOK_MIN_CARRIERS graze rule, excludeIds dedup, carriers), and anchor-state projection. The inactive-note test asserts a tier NUMBER, so it moves whenever the tier enum is renumbered — it went 3 to 2 on 2026-07-30 when staleness left the tier. This suite is the reason the v2.2.9 graze rule shipped in its refined form: a blunt two-carrier rule failed 7 of these tests, all single-carrier cases prior calibration deliberately protects.

summary: Live retrieval tests over a real seeded notebook — the hook-mode admission contracts live here, so this is the file that tells you whether a ranking change is intentional or a regression. Two things to know before editing. First, most tests here call kbSearch WITHOUT notesIndex, which means convergence cannot fire and every hit is name-channel-only; a change that penalises name-only hits will fail tests that look unrelated (stemming, matcher repairs) for that reason alone rather than because stemming broke. Second, 'convergence stands alone only when the term is also rare' asserted the OPPOSITE contract until 2026-07-31 — it was named 'convergence bypasses the suppression gate' and its setup deliberately pushes a term out of the rare band with six body-only decoy notes so that convergence is the only thing that could admit it. That exact shape is now the junk case, so the test asserts both halves: common+converged stays suppressed, rare+converged still injects on a single carrier. If you are relaxing the rarity requirement, this test is the one that should stop you.
